newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mostly firm on soybeans, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mostly firm on soybeans, exports.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mostly higher on better-than-expected exports, a rally in soybeans and potential harvest delays, traders said.
"They were all good numbers," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co, referring to USDA's weekly export inspections report.
USDA early Monday said corn export inspections for the week ended October 24 were at 35.153 million bushels, up from trade expectations for 25 million to 28 million bushels.
But traders noted the corn export pace continues to lag the year-ago weekly rate of 44.636 million bushels.
Showers forecast for this week could slow corn harvesting but the December contract failed to react with bullish enthusiasm.
"The bulk of the harvesting is ahead of us and that's why December couldn't work higher," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Technical traders said the moving averages in the December remain bearish.
Corn closed unchanged to four cents per bushel higher, with December unchanged at $2.75-1/4.
First resistance in the December was at $2.76-1/2 per bushel which was the session high.
The session low was $2.74-1/4 which was near first support in the December at $2.74-1/2.

December remained short term oversold with the nine day relative strength index closing at 23.933 points. Technical traders generally consider an RSI of 30 or less as oversold and 70 or more as overbought.

Traders noted Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report which showed non-commercials, including funds, short corn by roughly a two to one ratio as of October 22. Fund shorts on that date totaled 223.870 million bushels and longs totaled 111.1 million.
The number of non-commercial shorts increased by 19.91 million bushels since October 8 and the tally for longs decreased by 37.235 million bushels.
Key players included O'Connor and Co with three million bushels bought in the March, Cargill Inc and Merrill Lynch Futures each sold two million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 50,000 contracts, down from 60,504 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, LFG Futures bought 500 December $3.00 calls at 1/2 cent, Continental Grain bought 500 December $2.70 puts and sold 250 December $3.00 puts at 17-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, down from 28,709 Friday.
